newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia welcomes ex-Yugoslav asset agreement.
newsitem.headline: Croatia welcomes ex-Yugoslav asset agreement.

text.p: The National Bank of Croatia welcomed an agreement by four ex-Yugoslav central bank governors in Skopje on how to split some $600 million in federal gold and other pre-1991 Yugoslav assets.

"It is very important that a joint stance was taken...on the division of gold reserves, deposits and member shares in the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) of Basle," governor Marko Skreb said in a statement.
Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia accepted the division of joint assets among successor states according to their respective share in former Yugoslavia's gross domestic product (GDP).
A similar criterion was used in accords Croatia and Slovenia have reached with creditors on federal liabilities.
Skreb said he expected all relevant Croatian institutions to back up the decision taken by the four governors. No representative of rump Yugoslavia attended the meeting.
The accord was also expected to help central banks of the four ex-Yugoslav republics gain membership in the BIS, which initiated the talks on assets.
"We are eagar for the National Bank of Croatia to become a full member of BIS as soon as possible," Skreb added. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
